name: Prucalopride
sections: Unlike earlier 5-HT4 agonists (cisapride, tegaserod), prucalopride is highly selective and has no clinically relevant hERG/QT effect. First approval/introduction: Discovered by Janssen; EU 2009 (Movetis/Shire); Canada 2011; US FDA December 2018.

High-affinity selective 5-HT4 agonist that stimulates colonic peristalsis (high-amplitude propagating contractions), increasing bowel movement frequency in chronic constipation. Receptor / target profile: Selective, high-affinity 5-HT4 agonist (>150-fold selectivity over other receptors), stimulating colonic high-amplitude propagating contractions.
Summary: Bioavailability >90%; Tmax 2–3 h. ~30% protein bound. Mostly excreted unchanged in urine. Half-life ~24 h.
Chronic idiopathic constipation in adults in whom laxatives fail to provide adequate relief
Elderly (>65 years): start 1 mg once daily; increase to 2 mg if needed
Severe renal (CrCl <30) or hepatic impairment: 1 mg once daily
Re-evaluate if no benefit after 4 weeks
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Intestinal perforation or obstruction, obstructive ileus
Severe inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's, ulcerative colitis, toxic megacolon)
Suicidal ideation/behaviour reported – stop if mood worsens
Severe diarrhoea – may reduce oral contraceptive efficacy
Severe renal (CrCl <30) or hepatic impairment – 1 mg dose
Camilleri et al., NEJM 2008 – prucalopride 2–4 mg increased spontaneous complete bowel movements in severe chronic constipation.
Headache on the first day is common
Use contraception (diarrhoea may reduce pill efficacy)
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
